messages:
Anya: quick thought — instead of bolting another central orchestrator for canary/A-B rollouts, what if we try a lightweight choreography 'sentinel' that lives in the mesh and coordinates probes + fallback decisions?
Mike: can you sketch the win here vs the existing controller?
Anya: fewer cross-service RPCs, localised decisions, faster failover. sentinel runs near the sidecar, aggregates local probe signals, applies per-tenant hysteresis and emits a short verdict. Global coordinator only handles policy and audit.
Priya: :thinking: sounds promising but how do we ensure consistent view across nodes? split-brain risks?
Anya: sentinel keeps only short-lived state (windowed probe history). consistency for global rollouts comes from the control plane policy + version ids. we accept eventual alignment; failovers are safe because fallback variants are backward compatible (same API surface).
SRE-Ravi: ops concern — how do we avoid cascading failovers when a noisy AZ produces bad probes?
Liam: we should include topology-aware dampening: per-az quorum + decay-based trust scoring. short code sketch: 
```yaml
canary_policy:
  window: 30s
  quorum: 2/3
  trust_decay: 0.5/hour
  rollback_budget: 5%
  probe_types:
    - latency_p50
    - error_rate
    - output_quality
```
Eve: rollback_budget is interesting — do you mean max percent of traffic we allow to flip back automatically over a period?
Anya: yes. budget is a global safety cap (control-plane configured) so sentinel can do fast micro-rollbacks locally but cannot exceed the budget without control-plane approval.
Mike: what about correctness/regression detection for models? output_quality is fuzzier than latency.
Priya: propose a two-stage probe scoring: lightweight blackbox checks (latency/error) for instant fallback, and a slower semantic eval sweep (batch eval, prompt sets) that can trigger policy changes and alert humans.
SRE-Ravi: telemetry contract? we need structured probe events for postmortem.
Anya: agreed. sentinel emits compact events: {policy_id, decision, reason_codes, sample_keys}. keep payloads small to avoid high-cardinality metrics.
Liam: how do we handle KV cache priming/stateful sessions during rollbacks? large seq-length priming costs could make instant fallback expensive.
Eve: suggestion: use warmup escrow — when routing to canary, duplicate a small % of traffic to shadow warming nodes; sentinel tracks warmup_completion flag before increasing canary weight.
Priya: we should also add a 'graceful-deg' fallback that returns a lower-cost quantized model instead of full rollback, so user experience degrades smoothly.
Mike: SDK/API change implications? we can't break existing clients.
Anya: no API changes. routing and fallback are internal; clients still call the same endpoint. only new observability fields (headers) for traces, optional.
deploy-bot: deploy event: canary v2 -> 1687504321 by @Anya (10% traffic). status: started.
SRE-Ravi: operational playbook note — add an automatic 'probe-blackout' detector for infra events (spike in container restarts) so sentinel suspends decisions during platform incidents.
Eve: good call. also add a manual 'hold' toggle in console for customer-initiated freezes.
Liam: want to surface a small RFC section about signal taxonomy: (1) platform signals (node/az health), (2) perf signals (latency/err), (3) semantic signals (eval score). each has different action policies.
Priya: agree. plus retention rules: keep semantic evals longer for regression tracking, but short-lived for perf.
Mike: testing plan? we should run a staged experiment in staging with synthetic regressions and noisy az scenarios.
Anya: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with sequence diagrams, sentinel config schema, and an opt-in migration path. expect it by EOW.
Priya: thanks — happy to prototype the semantic eval hook.
SRE-Ravi: I'll add the blackout detector and chaos test cases.
Eve: +1 on warmup escrow. can we mock a priming budget for big-context models?
Liam: yes — include warmup_budget in policy, default small.
Mike: sounds good. small nit — need to explicitly document observability SLOs (event latency for sentinel decisions).
Anya: noted. will include observability SLOs and example dashboards.
Eve: one last thing — consider exposing a read-only debug endpoint for sentinels so oncall can quickly see local decisions without going to central logs.
Anya: good ops UX idea. thanks all, will send RFC link when ready: https://rfc.internal/r/placeholder-canary-sentinel
Mike: :rocket:
